title: 7-round AES-128: herd filter, near-codebook cp for selected subkey recovery

target.description: AES-128 reduced to 7 rounds on 128-bit blocks; initial AddRoundKey k^(0), then rounds 1 through 7, with no MixColumns in the final round. The described test selects four bytes of k^(0), four selected bytes of k^(7), and one byte of k'^(6), using an integral at b^(5). The known-text and selected-text endpoints have different access requirements.

setting.key_relation: One unknown master key with the standard AES expansion; no related-key access.
setting.key_population: general secret key; no weak-key restriction reported
setting.plaintext_model: Selected near-codebook: four plaintext bytes cover 2^32-2^23 chosen values; the remaining twelve bytes cover every value, totaling 2^128-2^119 distinct plaintexts.
assumptions: Wrong-subkey rejection uses the paper's heuristic model for zero XOR sums; no numerical whole-procedure success rate is supplied.

The paper presents these constructions as attacks on Rijndael. This record prices the explicitly analyzed selected-subkey filter; complete master-key reconstruction and any repeated filter applications are left for a separate completion-budget review.
Use only undamaged herds after removing the selected 2^23 four-byte values; approximately 2^23 complete three-fixed-byte herds remain.

time.note: The dominating scan updates one counter for each known/selected text. The paper uses 2^8 memory lookups per trial-encryption equivalent. Data acquisition is not counted as 2^128 new trial encryptions; scan operations and oracle observations remain separate.

data.note: This is (2^32-2^23)*2^96 selected distinct plaintexts. It is not a random known-plaintext sample.

memory.note: Section 2.5 gives the dominant 2^64 one-bit parity-counter array; later phases have smaller 2^32 counters. The near-codebook change is stated not to alter the attack complexity.

preprocessing.note: Table preparation and setup are described within the construction but not separately priced for this endpoint.

success.description: The exact partial_key_recovery endpoint has no numerical joint success. The zero sum over the entire unpartitioned codebook also holds for wrong guesses and is not a distinguisher; the attack uses correctly partitioned complete herds. The near-codebook construction leaves about half of the herds undamaged, a coverage count rather than a random-selection success rate. The source gives qualitative wrong-hypothesis rejection and an author headline, not a finite-budget probability for all targeted key material.

review.scope: Exact-edition endpoint-specific success audit; preserve resource parameters, existing conflicts and full-audit gates. Local source models and conditional relations do not certify whole-output success.

components.description: PDF6–9 Sections2.5–2.6: within a complete herd formed using the correct initial key hypothesis, the targeted byte of b5 sums to zero. For near-codebook data this is conditional on selecting an undamaged herd; it is not a claim about randomly choosing one.

evidence.interpretation: The budget is tied to the stated selected-subkey computation and native operation units. Broad headline claims are retained in the audit report without silently converting a selected-subkey budget into complete master-key recovery.
